fi-ctenochaetus-binotatus.title: Two Spot Bristletooth Tang
fi-ctenochaetus-binotatus.summary: A bristletooth tang that grazes film algae.
rows: About 8 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 22 cm (8.7 in) TL (FishBase)
Aggressive toward other tangs; peaceful with other fish
Herbivore. Offer seaweed (clipped or tied to rock) at least 3 times a week plus algae-based foods
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Tuamoto Islands, north to southern Japan, south to central New South Wales (Australia) and New Caledonia

fi-paracanthurus-hepatus.title: Blue Hippo Tang
fi-paracanthurus-hepatus.summary: The Pacific blue tang: electric blue with a black "painter's palette" marking. Active and needs room to swim.
rows: About 12 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 31 cm (12.2 in) TL (FishBase)
Aggressive toward its own species; to keep several, add them all at once to a large tank
Herbivore. Plenty of marine seaweed and algae foods, plus meaty foods
Indo-Pacific: East Africa, including the Mascarene Islands to Kiribati, north to southern Japan, south to the southern Great Barrier Reef, New Caledonia, and Samoa
notes: Likes a hiding spot among the rocks.

fi-acanthurus-lineatus.title: Clown (Lineatus) Tang
fi-acanthurus-lineatus.summary: A striped surgeonfish that needs very clean, well-oxygenated water.
rows: About 15 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 38 cm (15 in) TL (FishBase)
Aggressive toward other tangs and similar-shaped fish
Herbivore. Plenty of seaweed and algae foods
Indo-Pacific: East Africa, including the Mascarene Islands to the Hawaiian, Marquesas and Tuamoto islands, north to southern Japan

fi-ctenochaetus-tominiensis.title: Tomini Tang
fi-ctenochaetus-tominiensis.summary: A small bristletooth tang with a blue tail and golden-tipped fins when mature.
rows: About 6 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 16 cm (6.3 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Aggressive toward other tangs; peaceful with other fish
Herbivore. Seaweed and algae foods; grazes film algae
Western Central Pacific: Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, northern Great Barrier Reef, Solomon Islands, Palau, Vanuatu and Fiji

fi-acanthurus-nigrofuscus.title: Lavender Tang
fi-acanthurus-nigrofuscus.summary: A lavender-brown surgeonfish with orange cheek spots and a forked tail.
rows: About 8 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 21 cm (8.3 in) TL (FishBase)
Aggressive toward other tangs; peaceful with other fish
Herbivore. Seaweed and algae foods; grazes live rock
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea south to Transkei, South Africa and east to the Hawaiian and Tuamoto islands, north to southern Japan, south to the southern Great Barrier Reef

fi-acanthurus-tristis.title: Mimic Eibli Tang
fi-acanthurus-tristis.summary: A tang named for the way it mimics the look of Eibl's angelfish. Helps control algae.
rows: About 10 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 25 cm (9.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Very aggressive toward other tangs; keep only one except in very large systems
Indian Ocean: Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea west to Maldives and Chagos Archipelago, and east to islands of southern Indonesia at least to Bali

fi-naso-lituratus.title: Naso Tang (Orangespine Unicornfish)
fi-naso-lituratus.summary: A large unicornfish-family tang that needs lots of swimming room.
rows: About 18 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 46 cm (18.1 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Aggressive toward other tangs; peaceful with other fish
East Indian Ocean from Christmas Pacific Ocean: Honshu, Japan south to the Great Barrier Reef and New Caledonia and east to the Hawaiian Islands, French Polynesia
warn: May jump; keep a tight lid.

fi-acanthurus-olivaceus.title: Orangeshoulder Tang
fi-acanthurus-olivaceus.summary: A brown tang with an orange shoulder bar. Juveniles are solid yellow.
rows: About 14 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 35 cm (13.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Not usually aggressive toward other tangs
Pacific Ocean: Christmas Island and Cocos-Keeling Islands in the eastern Indian Ocean to the Hawaiian and Tuamoto islands, north to Japan, south to Lord Howe Island

fi-acanthurus-japonicus.title: Powder Brown Tang
fi-acanthurus-japonicus.summary: A popular surgeonfish for larger reef or fish-only tanks.
rows: About 8 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 23 cm (9.1 in) TL (FishBase)
Similar-shaped tangs can be very aggressive to each other
Indo-West Pacific: Sulawesi (Indonesia) to Philippines and Ryukyu Islands

fi-acanthurus-tennenti.title: Tennenti (Lieutenant) Tang
fi-acanthurus-tennenti.summary: A surgeonfish that tends to get along with other tangs.
rows: About 14 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 31 cm (12.2 in) TL (FishBase)
Not usually aggressive toward other tangs
Indian Ocean: East Africa to Sri Lanka and the Lesser Sunda Islands of southern Indonesia

fi-naso-unicornis.title: Bluespine Unicorn Tang
fi-naso-unicornis.summary: A large unicornfish. Needs a very big tank as it grows.
rows: About 24 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 70 cm (27.6 in) FL (FishBase)
Aggressive toward its own kind; peaceful with other fish
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to the Hawaiian, Marquesas and Tuamoto islands, north to southern Japan, south to Lord Howe and Rapa islands

fi-acanthurus-pyroferus.title: Yellow Mimic Tang
fi-acanthurus-pyroferus.summary: A tang known for mimicking the Lemonpeel Angelfish.
rows: About 8 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 29 cm (11.4 in) TL (FishBase)
Aggressive toward other tangs; peaceful with other fish
Indo-Pacific: Seychelles to the Marquesas and Tuamoto islands, north to southern Japan, south to the Great Barrier Reef and New Caledonia

fi-acanthurus-nigricans.title: Gold Rim Tang
fi-acanthurus-nigricans.summary: A dark surgeonfish, also sold as the Whitecheek Tang.
rows: About 8 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 36 cm (14.2 in) FL (FishBase)
Aggressive toward other tangs; peaceful with other fish
Eastern Indian Ocean: known only from Cocos-Keeling Islands and Christmas Island

fi-zebrasoma-scopas.title: Scopas Tang
fi-zebrasoma-scopas.summary: A brown tang covered in fine light-blue markings, with a brown tail.
rows: About 12 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 40 cm (15.7 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Aggressive toward its own kind and other tangs; best one per tank
Herbivore. Plenty of seaweed and algae foods (clip or tie seaweed at least 3 times a week)
Indo-Pacific: East Africa, including the Mascarene Islands to the Tuamoto Islands, north to southern Japan, south to Lord Howe and Rapa islands
notes: Needs 125 gal or more of swimming room.

fi-acanthurus-chirurgus.title: Doctorfish Tang
fi-acanthurus-chirurgus.summary: A grey-blue surgeonfish with darker vertical bars from the western Atlantic (Massachusetts to Brazil). A grazer that needs a lot of swimming room.
rows: About 15.5 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 39 cm (15.4 in) TL (FishBase)
Omnivore. Foods: dried seaweed sheets, marine algae, spirulina flake, mysis shrimp, krill, mussels, brine shrimp
Western Atlantic: Massachusetts (USA), Bermuda, and the northern Gulf of Mexico to São Paulo, Brazil
notes: More than one Acanthurus only in a very large tank, added at the same time.

fi-acanthurus-leucosternon.title: Powder Blue Tang
fi-acanthurus-leucosternon.summary: A powder-blue surgeonfish with a yellow dorsal fin and black face from shallow Indian Ocean reef flats. Beautiful but demanding: a tireless swimmer that is territorial in a closed tank, especially over its grazing areas.
rows: About 9 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 54 cm (21.3 in) TL (FishBase)
Herbivore. Foods: dried seaweed sheets, spirulina-enriched flakes, herbivore pellets, marine macroalgae, frozen mysis shrimp, frozen brine shrimp
Indian Ocean: eastern Africa to the Andaman Sea, southwest Indonesia and Christmas Island; with range extended to Bali, Indonesia in Western Pacific
notes: Add it last (or near last) so it does not claim the tank first; other tangs are a risk.

fi-zebrasoma-velifer.title: Sailfin Tang
fi-zebrasoma-velifer.summary: A banded yellow-and-dark tang from the Indo-Pacific with a huge sail-like dorsal fin. It needs a large tank with lots of swimming room.
rows: About 15 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 40 cm (15.7 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Herbivore. Foods: spirulina flakes, herbivore pellets, dried nori sheets, seaweed sheets, blanched spinach, romaine lettuce, mysid shrimp, brine shrimp
Eastern Indian Ocean to the Pacific Ocean: Christmas Island and most of the East Indian region to South China Sea
notes: Gets along with most unrelated fish; add aggressive tankmates after it has settled and avoid very aggressive fish like large triggers.

fi-acanthurus-chronixis.title: Half Black Mimic Tang
fi-acanthurus-chronixis.summary: A surgeonfish that is bright yellow at the front and black toward the tail. Trade fish come from the Caroline Islands.
rows: About 10 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 28 cm (11 in) TL (FishBase)
Herbivore. Foods: dried marine seaweed, herbivore flake food, herbivore pellets, blanched spinach, blanched zucchini, marine algae
Western Pacific: Kapingamarangi Atoll, Caroline Islands
notes: Add several tangs at the same time rather than one to an established resident.

fi-acanthurus-coeruleus.title: Atlantic Blue Tang
fi-acanthurus-coeruleus.summary: A western Atlantic surgeonfish that changes color with age: juveniles are lemon yellow and adults turn deep blue. A grazer for a big tank with high flow.
rows: About 12 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 39 cm (15.4 in) TL (FishBase)
Herbivore. Foods: marine algae, dried nori, spirulina, vegetable flakes, frozen herbivore preparations
Western Atlantic: New York, USA and Bermuda to the Gulf of Mexico and Brazil
notes: Usually fine with corals, but hungry fish have been seen picking at them, so keep it well fed with algae.
